source.markdown: ## ABSTRACT
source.text: ABSTRACT

blocks.text: ABSTRACT

target.markdown: ## 摘要

source.markdown: Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) are rapidly dominating the accelerator space, as illustrated by their wide-spread adoption in the data analytics and machine learning markets. At the same time, performance per watt has emerged as a crucial evaluation metric together with peak performance. As such, GPU architects require robust tools that will enable them to model both the performance and the power consumption of modern GPUs. However, while GPU performance modeling has progressed in great strides, power modeling has lagged behind. To mitigate this problem we propose AccelWatch, a configurable GPU power model that resolves two long-standing needs: the lack of a detailed and accurate cycle-level power model for modern GPU architectures, and the inability to capture their constant and static power with existing tools. AccelWatch can be driven by emulation and trace-driven environments, hardware counters, or a mix of the two, models both PTX and SASS ISAs, accounts for power gating and control-flow divergence, and supports DVFS. We integrate AccelWatch with GPGPU-Sim and Accel-Sim to facilitate its widespread use. We validate AccelWatch on a NVIDIA Volta GPU, and show that it achieves strong correlation against hardware power measurements. Finally, we demonstrate that AccelWatch can enable reliable design space exploration: by directly applying AccelWatch tuned for Volta on GPU configurations resembling NVIDIA Pascal and Turing GPUs, we obtain accurate power models for these architectures.

target.markdown: 图形处理器（GPU）正快速主导加速器领域，其在数据分析与机器学习市场中的广泛采用便是有力例证。与此同时，性能每瓦特与峰值性能一同成为至关重要的评估指标。因此，GPU 架构师需要稳健的工具，以便对现代 GPU 的性能与功耗进行建模。然而，尽管 GPU 性能建模已取得长足进步，功耗建模却相对滞后。为缓解这一问题，我们提出了 AccelWatch——一种可配置的 GPU 功耗模型，旨在满足两项长期需求：其一，现有工具缺乏针对现代 GPU 架构的细致且精确的周期级功耗模型；其二，现有工具无法刻画其恒定功耗与静态功耗。AccelWatch 可由模拟与追踪驱动环境、硬件计数器，或二者的混合驱动，能够同时建模 PTX 与 SASS 指令集，支持电源门控与控制流分化，并兼容 DVFS。我们将 AccelWatch 与 GPGPU-Sim 和 Accel-Sim 集成，以促进其广泛使用。我们在 NVIDIA Volta GPU 上对 AccelWatch 进行了验证，结果表明其与硬件功耗测量结果具有很强的相关性。最后，我们展示了 AccelWatch 可实现可靠的架构设计空间探索——直接将针对 Volta 调优的 AccelWatch 应用于类 NVIDIA Pascal 与 Turing GPU 的配置，即可获得这些架构的精确功耗模型。

target.markdown: ## 1 引言

source.markdown: Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) are becoming increasingly popular for accelerating both general-purpose and High-Performance Computing (HPC) applications. There are 147 GPU-accelerated systems in the most recent TOP500 HPC list [43], and 70% of the top-50 HPC applications are GPU-accelerated [40]. Similarly, GPUs have become one of the dominant forces in machine learning and AI acceleration [11]. As the proliferation of GPUs grows to satisfy the demand for higher performance, they are fast becoming a major consumer of power. Thus, it is not surprising that performance per watt, together with peak performance, have emerged as indispensable metrics for evaluating the efficiency of GPU architectures. As such, GPU architects require robust tools that will enable them to quickly and accurately model both the performance and the power consumption of modern GPUs.

source.markdown: Attempting to model recent GPUs such as Pascal [29], Volta [30] and Turing [31] using the methodology employed by GPUWatch produces significant inaccuracies, both in terms of absolute numbers and in terms of the relative power consumption of individual hardware components. This can lead to inadvertently optimizing components that may not be as important for energy efficiency in real systems as the model may allude. We find that a key source of errors is the lack of a model for Dynamic Voltage and Frequency

# AccelWatch Power Modeling Framework

## 1. Constant Power Modeling
- **Input**: μbenchmarks for dynamic power modeling
- **Output**: Feeds into Dynamic Power Modeling (step ⑦) and final model assembly (step )

---

## 2. Static Power Modeling

### 2.1 Divergence-Aware Static Power Modeling
- **Input**: μbenchmarks for divergence-aware static power modeling
- **Process**:
  - Analytic modeling → Divergence-aware static power model
- **Output**: Final static power model (step ④)

### 2.2 Idle-SM Static Power Modeling
- **Input**: μbenchmarks for idle-SM static power modeling
- **Process**:
  - Analytic modeling → Idle SM static power model
- **Output**: Feeds into Final static power model (step ④)

> **Note**: Steps ② and ③ converge at step ④ to produce the “Final static power model”.

---

## 3. Performance Modeling (Step ⑥)

### Input Selection
- Select perf. model:
  - SIM SASS → Accl-Sim, SASS
  - SIM PTX → Accl-Sim, PTX
  - HYBRID → HW perf. counters + Accl-Sim

### Hardware Measurements
- HW → Hardware perf. counters
- Output: Activity factors, #SMs, #lanes, instruction mix, #cycles, Vdd, f

### Output
- Feeds into:
  - AccelWatch power modeling
  - Dynamic power modeling (via hardware power measurements)

---

## 4. μBenchmarks for Dynamic Power Modeling (Step ⑤)

### Workflow
1. Start with μbenchmarks
2. Perform Hardware profiling
3. Decision: Need refinement?
   - **Yes** → Loop back to μbenchmarks
   - **No** → Proceed to “Final μbenchmarks set for dynamic power modeling”

### Output
- Final μbenchmarks set for dynamic power modeling → feeds into Dynamic Power Modeling (step ⑦)

---

## 5. Dynamic Power Modeling (Step ⑦)

### Quadratic Programming Module
- Components:
  - Quadratic optimization solver
  - Solver constraints
  - New scaling factors
  - Initial Scaling Factors (starting point S.)

### Decision Point: Can we do better?
- **Yes** → Iterate within quadratic programming loop
- **No** → Proceed to final model assembly (step ⑧)

### Power Component Maps
#### SASS → Power component map
- `"FADD"` → FPU_add
- `"IMUL"` → ALU_mul
- ...

#### PTX → Power component map
- `"add.s32"` → FPU_add
- `"mul.f64"` → DPU_mul
- ...

> These maps feed into AccelWatch power modeling and validation.

---

## 6. Validation (Step ⑨)

### Inputs
- Validation kernels
- Performance model runs
- Activity factors, #SMs, #lanes, instruction mix, #cycles, Vdd, f
- Hardware power measurements
- Technology scaling from Volta to target architecture

### Process
1. Run performance models on validation kernels
2. Extract activity metrics
3. Use hardware power measurements as ground truth
4. Apply technology scaling
5. Generate AccelWatch config files
6. Run AccelWatch modeling

### Output
- **Validated AccelWatch power model**

---

## 7. Final Model Assembly (Step ⑧)

### AccelWatch Power Model Composition
Combines three components:
- Constant power
- Static power
- Dynamic power

> All three are outputs of prior modules (steps , ④, ⑦ respectively).

---

## 8. Overall Flow Summary

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Constant power modeling] --> H[AccelWatch Power Model]
    B[Static power modeling] --> C[Divergence-aware] & D[Idle-SM]
    C --> E[Final static power model]
    D --> E
    E --> H
    F[μbenchmarks for dynamic power modeling] --> G[Performance modeling]
    G --> I[Hardware power measurements]
    I --> J[Dynamic power modeling]
    J --> K{Can we do better?}
    K -- Yes --> J
    K -- No --> H
    L[Validation] --> M[Validated AccelWatch power model]
    H --> L
    M --> N[AccelWatch config files]
    N --> O[AccelWatch modeling]
    O --> M
```

*(Note: Mermaid diagram is illustrative; actual flow follows numbered steps above.)*

---

## Key Abbreviations & Terms

- **μbenchmarks**: Micro-benchmarks used for characterization
- **SASS/PTX**: GPU assembly / intermediate representation
- **SIM/HYBRID**: Simulation modes (software-only or hybrid with hardware counters)
- **Vdd, f**: Supply voltage and frequency
- **#SMs, #lanes**: Number of Streaming Multiprocessors and execution lanes
- **Activity factors**: Utilization metrics per functional unit
- **Quadratic programming**: Optimization technique for fitting dynamic power coefficients
- **Technology scaling**: Adjusting model parameters across GPU architectures (e.g., Volta → Ampere)

Our insight, that power under V-F scaling is better modeled by a  $ 3^{rd} $ -degree polynomial missing a quadratic term (Section 4.2), allows AccelWatch to accurately estimate constant power.

target.markdown: 动态电压频率调节（DVFS）。缺乏 DVFS 模型会导致在描述现代 GPU 时出现负的恒定功耗项。我们的洞见在于：在 V-F 调节下的功耗更适于用一个缺少二次项的三次多项式来建模（第 4.2 节），这使得 AccelWatch 能够准确地估计恒定功耗。

source.markdown: Another key source of error is the lack of a model for capturing the power-down of hardware components, and their contribution to static power when powered-up but inactive. In the absence of such a model, static power is lumped into a single constant, an oversimplification for modern chips with aggressive power gating. We infer, for the first time to our knowledge, how modern GPUs power-gate chip-wide hardware components (e.g., L2 cache), Streaming Multiprocessor (SM)-wide components (e.g., L1 caches) and lane-specific components (e.g., FPUx). AccelWatch accurately models the effect of reactivating power-gated structures. It does so by capitalizing on our insights (Section 4.3) that: (1) activating the first SM powers up global chip components which leak when not switching; (2) activating the first lane of an SM powers up SM-wide components, which leak when inactive; and (3) activating subsequent lanes additionally powers up only those lanes' execution units. Our insight, that the simultaneous execution of operations within a warp (now supported by modern GPUs [30]) presents a counter-intuitive sawtooth pattern of power consumption (Section 4.4), allows AccelWatch to accurately model thread divergence in the presence of Instruction-Level Parallelism (ILP) (Section 4.5).

target.markdown: 另一个关键的误差来源在于缺少对硬件组件断电以及组件在加电但空闲时对静态功耗贡献的建模。若缺乏此类模型，静态功耗会被合并为一个常数，这对具有激进电源门控的现代芯片而言过于简化。据我们所知，我们首次推断出现代 GPU 如何对全芯片级硬件组件（例如 L2 缓存）、流多处理器（SM）级组件（例如 L1 缓存）以及通道级组件（例如 FPUx）进行电源门控。AccelWatch 能够准确建模重新激活被门控结构所带来的影响。这得益于我们的若干洞见（第 4.3 节）：（1）激活第一个 SM 会开启全局芯片组件，这些组件在不进行开关操作时会泄漏功耗；（2）激活某个 SM 的首个通道会开启该 SM 级组件，这些组件在空闲时同样会泄漏功耗；（3）激活后续通道则仅额外开启这些通道自身的执行单元。我们的另一项洞见——同一 warp 内操作的同时执行（现代 GPU 已支持该特性 [30]）呈现出反直觉的锯齿状功耗模式（第 4.4 节）——使 AccelWatch 能够在存在指令级并行（ILP）的条件下准确建模线程分化（第 4.5 节）。

source.markdown: Some recently-proposed power models [2, 13, 47] target modern GPUs, but they, as well as earlier works [16, 50] are provided only as analytic models over average behavior, which hinders research that requires cycle-level accuracy (e.g., research on DVFS). Moreover, analytic models are hard to extend to describe novel architectural components; often it is easier to build a cycle-level model that emulates the component's behavior and use it for evaluation. To support cycle-level research, the computer architecture community needs a robust and configurable power modeling tool, capable of supporting cycle-accurate simulation.

source.markdown: our knowledge, AccelWatch is the only power model capable of modeling both PTX (virtual ISA) and SASS (native machine ISA) instructions, and the only open-source tool capable of modeling closed-source workloads with hand-tuned SASS instructions—it only needs a binary. target.markdown: 据我们所知，AccelWatch 是目前唯一能够同时对 PTX（虚拟 ISA）和 SASS（原生机器 ISA）指令进行功耗建模的工具，也是唯一能够对含有手工调优 SASS 指令的闭源工作负载进行建模的开源工具——它只需要一个二进制文件即可。此外，AccelWatch 还是目前唯一既可由纯软件性能模型（例如 Accel-Sim [20]）驱动，也可由现代 GPU 中常见的硬件性能计数器驱动（从而捕获真实芯片上的执行情况），或由二者结合驱动的 GPU 功耗模型。这些 AccelWatch 变体使研究人员能够在功耗模型的精度与性能建模工作量之间进行权衡。

source.markdown: We validate AccelWatch against hardware power measurements on an NVIDIA Volta GV100 [30] GPU running a suite of 26 kernels from NVIDIA CUDA Samples [35], Rodinia 3.1 [7], Parboil [41], and CUTLASS 1.3 [32] suites. AccelWatch yields a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE [9]) between 7.5–9.2±2.1–3.1%, depending on the AccelWatch variant, achieving a Pearson r coefficient of 0.83–0.91. These errors are a factor of 22–24× lower than GPUWatch's when targeting the same architecture. As a case study, we apply AccelWatch on kernels from DeepBench [25] workloads, and find that it obtains 12.79% MAPE over hardware power measurements despite the significant limitations of existing performance models. We demonstrate the reliability of AccelWatch for design space exploration by applying our validated AccelWatch Volta model (i.e., without retraining or needing new hardware measurements) to model the power of two GPU architectures: a Pascal TITAN X [29], and a Turing RTX 2060S [31]. AccelWatch accurately predicts the power consumption of these new architectures, achieving 11 ± 3.8% and 13 ± 4.7% MAPE, respectively.

target.markdown: ## 2 ACCELWATTCH 建模工作流程

source.markdown: We follow the process shown in Figure 1 to develop a model that accurately estimates: (a) constant power, for example by board fans and peripheral circuitry, in the presence of DVFS ①; (b) static power in the presence of execution divergence, the simultaneous execution of operations within the same warp [30], variability in SM occupancy, and the power gating of lanes, SMs, and global chip hardware components ②–④; and (c) dynamic power consumption for each individual hardware component ⑤–⑧. To model dynamic power, we develop a suite of 102 microbenchmarks that isolate and stress the various components of a modern GPU ⑤. We use them, together with hardware power measurements and execution statistics ⑥, to bound any modeling inaccuracies using quadratic programming ⑦. AccelWatch is driven by a performance model, which provides AccelWatch with statistics on hardware component activity, active SMs and lanes, voltage-frequency parameters, and cycle count ⑥. We integrate AccelWatch with GPGPU-Sim [3] and Accel-Sim [20] to facilitate its use for both PTX [37] and SASS [36] simulations, producing the AccelWatch PTX SIM and AccelWatch SASS SIM variants, respectively.

target.markdown: 我们按照图 1 所示的过程开发模型，以准确估算：(a) 在 DVFS 存在情况下的恒定功耗（例如板载风扇和外设电路的功耗）①；(b) 在执行分化、同一 warp 内操作同时执行 [30]、SM 占用率变化以及 lane、SM 和全局芯片硬件组件的电源门控存在情况下的静态功耗 ②–④；以及 (c) 每个独立硬件组件的动态功耗 ⑤–⑧。为了建模动态功耗，我们开发了一套由 102 个微基准测试组成的测试集，用于隔离并压力测试现代 GPU 的各个组件 ⑤。我们将这些微基准测试与硬件功耗测量及执行统计信息 ⑥ 结合，使用二次规划来界定建模误差的上界 ⑦。AccelWatch 由性能模型驱动，性能模型为其提供有关硬件组件活动、活跃 SM 与 lane、电压-频率参数以及周期数等统计信息 ⑥。我们将 AccelWatch 与 GPGPU-Sim [3] 和 Accel-Sim [20] 集成，以便同时支持 PTX [37] 和 SASS [36] 仿真，分别生成 AccelWatch PTX SIM 和 AccelWatch SASS SIM 两种变体。

source.markdown: AccelWatch can also be driven by hardware performance counters collected during execution on real silicon, either entirely (AccelWatch HW) or in combination with software-modelled ones (AccelWatch HYBRID). This allows for the study of discrete hardware components without the need to develop accurate software performance models for the entire architecture. Building comprehensive and accurate performance models for GPUs is a painstaking and time-consuming process. In the absence of sophisticated software performance models like Accel-Sim [20] for future GPUs, one can use hardware performance counters and execution on real silicon to model the power of a GPU architecture, and replace the hardware performance counters of the component targeted by the research with counters obtained from a model of only that component.

In the absence of sophisticated software performance models like Accel-Sim [20] for future GPUs, one can use hardware performance counters and execution on real silicon to model the power of a GPU architecture, and replace the hardware performance counters of the component targeted by the research with counters obtained from a model of only that component.

target.markdown: AccelWatch 也可以由真实芯片上执行期间采集的硬件性能计数器完全驱动（AccelWatch HW），或与软件建模的计数器结合驱动（AccelWatch HYBRID）。这使得研究人员能够在无需为整个体系结构开发精确软件性能模型的情况下，对离散的硬件组件进行研究。为 GPU 构建全面且精确的性能模型是一项艰辛且耗时的过程。在缺少像 Accel-Sim [20] 这样成熟的软件性能模型来支持未来 GPU 的情况下，可以借助硬件性能计数器与真实芯片上的执行来对 GPU 架构进行功耗建模，并将研究目标组件的硬件性能计数器替换为仅针对该组件的模型所提供的计数器。

Then, a performance model provides AccelWatch with the kernel's execution statistics (e.g., through simulation or hardware counters from execution on real silicon) ⑨. If needed, the resulting power estimates are scaled to a new technology node.

source.markdown: A salient feature of AccelWatch is its longevity. As architectures and technology continue to evolve, power modeling tools must adapt to match their target systems. Our power modeling framework is equipped with a suite of microbenchmarks, analytical models, an optimization solver, and a validation methodology that can support future GPUs.

source.markdown: GPUs execute programs known as "kernels", which comprise several threads, often thousands. Threads do not execute instructions independently; rather, sets of 32 threads (warps) execute the same instruction on different data by using their thread ID to select the data items to work on.

target.markdown: GPU 执行被称为"内核"的程序，这些程序由大量线程（通常数以千计）组成。线程并非独立执行指令，而是以 32 个线程为一组（warp），通过各自的线程 ID 选择待处理的数据项，从而在不同的数据上执行相同的指令。

source.markdown: A Volta GV100 GPU chip consists of 80 Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs). Each SM is partitioned into four processing blocks [30], each with 16 INT32 cores for integer arithmetic, 16 FP32 and 8 FP64 cores for 32- and 64-bit floating-point, two tensor cores for matrix arithmetic, one special function unit (SFU) for complex operations (e.g., log), one warp scheduler, one dispatch unit, and a 64KB register file [30]. The INT32, FP32 and FP64 cores have adders, multipliers, and fused-multiply-add (FMA) units. The warp scheduler and dispatch unit can issue one instruction per clock to 32 execution lanes. Each of the 4 processing blocks per SM has 8 LD/ST units and a 12KB L0 instruction cache [19]. Each SM features a 128KB L1 data cache/shared memory, 2KB L1 and 64KB L1.5 constant caches, and a 128KB L1 instruction cache. The GPU has a 6144KB unified L2 cache at the chip level, and a 32GB GPU DRAM off chip [19].

target.markdown: 一颗 Volta GV100 GPU 芯片由 80 个流多处理器（SM）组成。每个 SM 被划分为四个处理块 [30]，每个处理块包含：16 个用于整数运算的 INT32 核心、16 个 FP32 核心与 8 个 FP64 核心（分别用于 32 位和 64 位浮点运算）、两个用于矩阵运算的 Tensor Core、一个用于复杂运算（例如 log）的特殊函数单元（SFU）、一个 warp 调度器、一个分派单元，以及一个 64 KB 的寄存器文件 [30]。INT32、FP32 和 FP64 核心均配备加法器、乘法器以及融合乘加（FMA）单元。warp 调度器和分派单元每个时钟可向 32 条执行 lane 分派一条指令。每个 SM 中的 4 个处理块各自配备 8 个 LD/ST 单元和一个 12 KB 的 L0 指令缓存 [19]。每个 SM 还包含一个 128 KB 的 L1 数据缓存/共享内存、2 KB 的 L1 与 64 KB 的 L1.5 常量缓存，以及一个 128 KB 的 L1 指令缓存。该 GPU 在芯片层面配备一个 6144 KB 的统一 L2 缓存，并在芯片外配备 32 GB 的 GPU DRAM [19]。

We ensure that the microbenchmarks present the desired behavior by profiling them using hardware performance counters provided by NVIDIA Nsight Compute [39].

source.markdown: To protect our experiments from the impact of temperature variations, we bring the GPU chip to 65°C before taking power measurements for a target kernel. Temperature variability affects static power exponentially. Keeping a constant temperature during hardware measurements eliminates this noise. After AccelWatch learns a model assuming constant temperature, one can model temperature variations by multiplying the modeled static power with an experimentally-derived temperature-dependent factor.

---

# 处理器频率与功耗关系图

## 图表概述

该图为**处理器频率（GHz） vs. 功耗（W）** 的多系列折线图，展示不同操作类型在随频率增加时的功耗变化趋势，并与“Modelled”（建模值）进行对比。

---

## 坐标轴

- **X 轴：Processor Frequency (GHz)**  
  范围：0.0 – 1.6 GHz  
  刻度间隔：0.2 GHz

- **Y 轴：Power (W)**  
  范围：0 – 250 W  
  刻度间隔：50 W  
  带有网格线辅助读数

---

## 数据系列与图例

| 图例标识       | 符号/颜色         | 含义             |
|----------------|-------------------|------------------|
| `INT_MEM`      | 绿色菱形 + 实线   | 整数内存操作     |
| `INT_ADD`      | 橙色方块 + 实线   | 整数加法操作     |
| `FP_ADD`       | 灰色三角形 + 实线 | 浮点加法操作     |
| `FP_MUL`       | 蓝色圆形 + 实线   | 浮点乘法操作     |
| `NANOSLEEP`    | 浅蓝倒三角 + 实线 | 纳秒级睡眠操作   |
| `Modeled`      | 红色虚线          | 理论建模功耗曲线 |

> 注：除 “Modeled” 外，其余均为实测或模拟的具体操作类型功耗；“Modeled” 为参考基准线。

---

## 数据趋势分析

### 1. 整体趋势
- 所有操作类型的功耗均随处理器频率升高而**非线性增长**。
- 在低频段（< 0.4 GHz），各操作功耗接近且较低（约 30–40 W）。
- 高频段（> 1.0 GHz），功耗差异显著扩大，尤其 `INT_MEM` 增长最快。

### 2. 各操作类型表现

#### ✅ INT_MEM（绿色菱形）
- 起始于 ~35 W @ 0.2 GHz
- 快速上升，在 1.4 GHz 达到 **~210 W**
- 是所有操作中功耗最高的，斜率最陡

#### ✅ INT_ADD（橙色方块）
- 起始于 ~35 W @ 0.2 GHz
- 在 1.4 GHz 达到 **~130 W**
- 增长速率次于 INT_MEM，但高于 FP 类操作

#### ✅ FP_MUL（蓝色圆形）
- 起始于 ~35 W @ 0.2 GHz
- 在 1.4 GHz 达到 **~120 W**
- 与 INT_ADD 接近，略低

#### ✅ FP_ADD（灰色三角形）
- 起始于 ~35 W @ 0.2 GHz
- 在 1.4 GHz 达到 **~110 W**
- 增长平缓，低于乘法和整数加法

#### ✅ NANOSLEEP（浅蓝倒三角）
- 起始于 ~35 W @ 0.2 GHz
- 在 1.4 GHz 仅达 **~55 W**
- 功耗最低，几乎呈线性缓慢增长

####  Modeled（红色虚线）
- 作为理论模型曲线，贯穿所有数据点下方或中间
- 在低频段贴合较好，高频段略低于实际测量值（如 INT_MEM）
- 表明实际功耗在高负载下超出简单模型预测

---

## 关键观察点

- **功耗非线性增长**：尤其在 >1.0 GHz 后，功耗加速上升，符合动态功耗公式 $P \propto C V^2 f$ 中频率项的影响。
- **操作类型影响显著**：内存密集型（INT_MEM）远高于计算密集型（FP_ADD/NANOSLEEP），反映访存开销大。
- **建模偏差**：红色虚线在高频区低估了部分操作（如 INT_MEM）的实际功耗，提示需更复杂模型（如考虑电压缩放、缓存命中失效等）。
- **NANOSLEEP 特殊性**：其功耗几乎不随频率剧烈变化，可能因 CPU 进入低功耗状态或指令本身无活跃计算。

---

## 结论建议

- 对于高性能场景（高频率），应优先优化内存访问模式以降低 INT_MEM 功耗。
- 建模工具需引入更多硬件行为参数（如缓存层级、分支预测失败率）以提升高频段精度。
- NANOSLEEP 可作为节能调度策略的有效手段，在空闲时段维持低频率即可大幅省电。

This methodology relies on scaling down the frequency $f$, which linearly reduces the first term (dynamic power). By running kernels at varying frequencies and measuring the GPU's power consumption each time, one could estimate this linear relationship. Extrapolating this line to $f = 0$ eliminates the $mCV^2f$ term and leaves only the $nP_{const}$ term, providing an estimate of the static and constant power.

# GPU Power Consumption Breakdown by Activation Level

## Chart Title: Measured Power (W) vs. Chip/SM/Lane Activation States

1. `Inactive Chip`
2. `1 Lane × 1 SM`
3. `1 Lane × 80 SMs`

| Color       | Component        |
|-------------|------------------|
| 🟦 Blue     | Const            |
| 🟧 Orange   | Chip Global      |
| ⬜ Gray     | SM Activation    |
| 🟨 Yellow   | Addl. Lanes      |

> *Note: “Addl. Lanes” = Additional Lanes activated beyond base configuration.*

---

## Annotations & Data Points:

### 1. Inactive Chip
- Total power ≈ **35 W**
- Composition: Only `Const` (blue) component active.

### 2. 1 Lane × 1 SM
- Total power ≈ **55 W**
- Annotation:  
  > `first 5M lane on chip (activating first SM)`  
  → Arrow points to orange segment (`Chip Global`) indicating activation of first Streaming Multiprocessor.
- Composition:
  - `Const`: ~35 W
  - `Chip Global`: ~20 W

### 3. 1 Lane × 80 SMs
- Total power ≈ **95 W**
- Annotation:  
  > `+79 lanes, 1 per SM (activating +79 SMs)`  
  → Arrow points to gray segment (`SM Activation`) indicating activation of additional 79 SMs.
- Composition:
  - `Const`: ~35 W
  - `Chip Global`: ~20 W
  - `SM Activation`: ~40 W

### 4. 8 Lanes × 80 SMs
- Total power ≈ **110 W**
- Annotation:  
  > `+560 lanes`  
  → Yellow segment added above gray.
- Composition:
  - `Const`: ~35 W
  - `Chip Global`: ~20 W
  - `SM Activation`: ~40 W
  - `Addl. Lanes`: ~15 W

### 5. 16 Lanes × 80 SMs
- Total power ≈ **125 W**
- Annotation:  
  > `+1200 lanes`
- Composition:
  - `Const`: ~35 W
  - `Chip Global`: ~20 W
  - `SM Activation`: ~40 W
  - `Addl. Lanes`: ~30 W

### 6. 24 Lanes × 80 SMs
- Total power ≈ **140 W**
- Annotation:  
  > `+1840 lanes`
- Composition:
  - `Const`: ~35 W
  - `Chip Global`: ~20 W
  - `SM Activation`: ~40 W
  - `Addl. Lanes`: ~45 W

- Total power ≈ **155 W**
- Annotation:  
  > `+2480 lanes`
- Composition:
  - `Const`: ~35 W
  - `Chip Global`: ~20 W
  - `SM Activation`: ~40 W
  - `Addl. Lanes`: ~60 W

## Observations:

- The `Const` component remains constant at ~35 W across all configurations — likely representing baseline static power.
- `Chip Global` activates with the first SM and remains fixed at ~20 W thereafter.
- `SM Activation` adds ~40 W when scaling from 1 SM to 80 SMs (i.e., activating 79 more SMs).
- `Addl. Lanes` scales linearly with number of lanes beyond 1 lane per SM:
  - From 1→8 lanes: +560 lanes → +15 W
  - From 8→16 lanes: +640 lanes → +15 W (total +30 W)
  - From 16→24 lanes: +640 lanes → +15 W (total +45 W)
  - From 24→32 lanes: +640 lanes → +15 W (total +60 W)

source.markdown: After estimating constant power, i.e., $P_{const}$ in Eq. (3), we next consider the second term, $\tau f$, which models static power. First, we turn our attention to modeling static power in the presence of power gating. We infer how modern GPUs are gating chip-wide, SM-wide and lane-specific hardware components. We measure the impact on power consumption of re-activating these components on real hardware, and introduce an analytic model that explains the power-gating behavior of GPUs and accurately captures their power consumption in the presence of power gating. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first time that the power-gating behavior of GPUs is inferred, measured and modeled analytically.

target.markdown: 在估计出恒定功耗（即公式 (3) 中的 $P_{const}$）之后，我们接下来考虑第二项 $\tau f$，该项用于建模静态功耗。首先，我们将注意力转向在存在功耗门控情况下的静态功耗建模。我们推断现代 GPU 是如何对全芯片级、SM 级以及 lane 级硬件组件进行门控的。我们在真实硬件上测量重新激活这些组件对功耗的影响，并引入一个分析模型来解释 GPU 的功耗门控行为，从而在存在功耗门控的情况下准确刻画其功耗。据我们所知，这是首次对 GPU 的功耗门控行为进行推断、测量与分析建模。

source.markdown: When lanes or SMs are inactive, modern GPUs gate them to conserve power. There are some components that all SMs share (e.g., L2 cache). These global chip components are powered up even when there is only one SM active on the GPU. When they are activated, these components leak power when they are not switching. Similarly, there are components that all lanes share in an SM (e.g., L1 caches, shared memory. These SM-wide components are active even when there is only one thread active in an SM, while the remaining lanes are power gated. These components also leak power when they are not switching. As additional lanes become active, they power up their own lane-specific functional units (e.g., INT32 and FP32 cores) which may also leak power when inactive.

target.markdown: 当 lane 或 SM 处于非活动状态时，现代 GPU 会对其进行功耗门控以节省功耗。所有 SM 共享的某些组件（例如 L2 缓存）属于全芯片级组件，即使 GPU 上仅有一个 SM 处于活动状态，这些组件仍会上电；它们在激活后即使不进行开关切换也会产生漏电功耗。同样，SM 内所有 lane 共享的某些组件（例如 L1 缓存、共享内存）属于 SM 级组件，即使 SM 内仅有一个线程处于活动状态，这些组件仍会保持激活，而其余 lane 则被功耗门控；这些组件在不切换时同样会产生漏电功耗。随着更多 lane 变为活动状态，它们会激活各自 lane 专有的功能单元（例如 INT32 和 FP32 核），这些单元在不工作时也可能产生漏电功耗。

source.markdown: Figure 3 shows the hardware-measured power of a microbenchmark that issues integer operations to a varying number of SMs and lanes per SM. When no SM is active on the chip, it consumes only constant power (estimated in Section 4.2). When the microbenchmark runs on only one lane on one SM (1 Lane × 1 SM), that first SM activation powers up that SM's structures, but also activates global chip structures shared by all SMs. When the microbenchmark utilizes additional SMs (1 Lane × 80 SMs), it additionally powers up only the SM-wide components of the additional SMs. As a result, the first activated SM on a GPU consumes 47× more power than each one of the subsequently-activated SMs. For example, 1 Lane × 80 SMs consumes 70% more power than 1 Lane × 1 SM, even though it utilizes 79× more SMs.

source.markdown: However, the linear model of Eq. (4) does not always match real-world observations. An SM in Volta comprises 4 processing blocks [30], each with 16 CUDA cores. A warp executes by running two 16-thread half-warps, one after the other. If a warp has $y \le 16$ threads active, the processing block executes the active half-warp but forgoes the execution of the empty one. Thus, the same fraction of lanes is active on every cycle, and the power consumption rises as $y$ grows. At $y = 16$, all 16 cores on all processing blocks are always active, consuming maximum power.

source.markdown: ### 4.5 ILP and Execution Divergence
source.text: 4.5 ILP and Execution Divergence

blocks.text: 4.5 ILP and Execution Divergence

target.markdown: ### 4.5 ILP 与执行分歧

source.markdown: When a kernel uses only one functional unit, power strongly follows the half-warp model (Figure 4a). When exercising two units, (e.g., when the kernel issues both INT32 and FP32 instructions—Figure 4b), the half-warp behavior is less pronounced. This happens because Volta can simultaneously execute operations in the same warp by running multiple functional units concurrently [30]. A kernel with ILP can exploit this behavior to execute faster. As different operations usually have different latencies, their executions become interleaved in time. Hence, on every cycle we observe a statistical mix of full and partial half-warps: if we take a snapshot of the GPU, we will observe processing blocks executing "full half-warps" (Section 4.4) of one instruction concurrently with "partial half-warps" of the other. This statistical mix smooths out the sawtooth-like pattern of power consumption. When more units are employed (Figure 4c) the behavior becomes almost purely linear. Thus, static power for active SMs gradually drifts from the half-warp to the linear model, depending on the instruction mix. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first time this behavior is inferred and modeled.

target.markdown: 当一个 kernel 仅使用一个功能单元时，功耗严格遵循半 warp 模型（图 4a）。而当使用两个功能单元时（例如当 kernel 同时发出 INT32 和 FP32 指令时——图 4b），半 warp 行为的特征就不再那么明显。这是因为 Volta 可以通过并行运行多个功能单元来同时执行同一 warp 中的操作 [30]。具有 ILP 的 kernel 可以利用这一特性来更快地执行。由于不同操作通常具有不同的延迟，它们的执行在时间上会交错进行。因此，在每个周期上，我们观察到完整半 warp 与部分半 warp 在统计意义上的混合：如果我们对 GPU 进行一次快照，会观察到处理块同时执行某个指令的"完整半 warp"（第 4.4 节）以及另一指令的"部分半 warp"。这种统计混合平滑了功耗中锯齿状的模式。当使用更多功能单元时（图 4c），其行为几乎完全变为线性。因此，活动 SM 的静态功耗会随着指令混合的不同，从半 warp 模型逐渐过渡到线性模型。据我们所知，这是首次推断并建模该行为。

source.markdown: Capitalizing on this observation, we assess the typical instruction patterns in GPU kernels and develop microbenchmarks that selectively stress them. We identified a total of 9 instruction mix categories, ranging from homogeneous categories with only integer ADD or only integer MUL instructions, to categories comprising a mix of instructions: int, int/FP, int/FP/DP, int/FP/SFU, int/FP/TEX, int/FP/tensor, and a category of only light instructions (e.g., nanosleep). We create the appropriate half-warp or linear models for each instruction mix and integrate them in AccelWatch. During an AccelWatch run, the performance model (simulator or hardware counters) reports the lane occupancy and instruction mix to AccelWatch, which then picks the appropriate power model.

(12) as a dot product between a vector of power coefficients $\hat{P}_i \cdot x_i, ..., P_{static,activeSM} \cdot 1, P_{idleSM} \cdot 1, P_{const} \cdot 1$ (which remain constant for a given GPU) and activity factors, $a_i, y$ and $k$, which vary across kernels. These vectors have $N + 3$ dimensions. $N$ components of the vectors relate to estimated dynamic power, where each component contains an unknown factor, $x_i$. The three remaining components (modeled in Section 4) relate to constant, static, and idle SM power (these components effectively have $x_i = 1$). A single kernel will produce a vector with $N + 3$ activity factors, which can be used to estimate that workload's power consumption on the GPU. A collection of $M$ kernels will provide $M \times (N + 3)$ set of equations, shown in Eq. (13). In this equation, the initially-inaccurate power estimates for the power components in $P_{est.}$ are corrected by the parameter vector $X$, to obtain a power for each kernel that approximates its hardware power measurement, $P_{meas}$.

target.markdown: 我们通过对 AccelSim v1.1.0 [20] 中集成的底层 GPGPU-Sim v4.0.1 [3] 所附带的、基于 McPAT [22] 的、长期未维护的 GPUWatch [21] 功耗模型进行大量修改，开发出了 AccelWatch。AccelWatch 由一个性能模型驱动，该性能模型向 AccelWatch 提供关于硬件组件活动、活动 SM 和 lane、电压-频率参数以及周期计数等方面的统计数据（图 1-(6)）。

source.markdown: For the performance model of AccelWatch variants driven fully or partially by software simulations (SASS SIM, PTX SIM, HYBRID) we use the latest publicly-available version of Accel-Sim v1.1.0 [20]. Accel-Sim has been extensively validated against Volta, showing strong performance correlation with > 0.97 Pearson r coefficient. For SASS simulations we feed Accel-Sim with SASS traces generated by the NVIDIA Binary Instrumentation Tool (NVBit) [45]. For PTX simulations, Accel-Sim invokes the underlying GPGPU-Sim.

target.markdown: 对于由软件模拟完全或部分驱动的 AccelWatch 各变体（SASS SIM、PTX SIM、HYBRID）的性能模型，我们使用最新公开可用的 Accel-Sim v1.1.0 [20] 版本。Accel-Sim 已针对 Volta 进行了广泛的验证，与实测性能具有很强的相关性，Pearson 相关系数大于 0.97。对于 SASS 模拟，我们将由 NVIDIA 二进制插桩工具（NVBit）[45] 生成的 SASS trace 输入到 Accel-Sim 中。对于 PTX 模拟，Accel-Sim 调用底层的 GPGPU-Sim。

source.markdown: At each sampling period (500 cycles) Accel-Sim provides execution statistics to AccelWatch, which uses them to estimate the workload's power for each sampling period. As the performance model provides AccelWatch with frequency and voltage settings at each sampling interval, AccelWatch can scale the estimated power for that interval following Eq. (2). Thus, if the performance model is DVFS-capable, AccelWatch will calculate all power transitions.

source.markdown: Following the process shown in Figure 1-⑤ and the methodology in Section 4.1, we build a suite of 102 microbenchmarks that stress target hardware components to estimate their power consumption. We use a mixture of compiler options, inline-assembly (PTX), and pointer-chasing (for microbenchmarks that stress the memory hierarchy) to work around default compiler optimizations. We place the Region of Interest (ROI) of these kernels inside an unrolled loop, and run them on silicon with a high loop iteration count.

source.markdown: Figure 6 shows the dynamic power heat-map of microbenchmarks based on the hardware component categories they target. Each cell's color encodes the fraction of dynamic power a microbenchmark spends on the corresponding GPU component, as estimated by AccelWatch SASS SIM. It is important to note that even if a hardware unit is stressed by continuously issuing instructions to it, other units may also be accessed with a high frequency (e.g., register file, L1i), and the power consumed by these other units may be higher than the targeted one's. In such cases, the heat-map cell corresponding to the targeted unit may not appear "hot". For example, this behavior appears with units that do not consume much power, e.g., the Texture Unit, or with microbenchmarks that stress the INT32 Core with highly-divergent code. Overall, the heat-map demonstrates that each microbenchmark exercises the corresponding GPU component it targets, and our suite adequately exercises all components.

#### 6. 结论

该热力图揭示了 GPU 微基准测试中各类别对硬件组件的依赖关系：

- 计算核心（INT32, FP32/64, SFU, Tensor）高度依赖自身的专用单元及通用资源（寄存器、DRAM）。
- 存储子系统（Register File, dCaches, DRAM）是所有工作负载的关键瓶颈或热点。
- “Mix” 类别体现实际应用的复杂性，需综合评估整个硬件栈性能。
- 此图可用于指导 GPU 架构优化、调度策略设计或功耗建模。

source.markdown: We use two different starting points for the scaling factors used in the initial iteration of this process. For one of the starting points, all initial scaling factors are set to one, thus there is no scaling taking place initially. The other starting point is obtained from the GPUWatch model for NVIDIA Fermi GTX 480 [27] which has been independently validated [21]. Due to having two starting points, we end up with two AccelWatch models. The model obtained from the Fermi starting point achieves higher accuracy (9.2% vs. 14.8% MAPE on the validation set for SASS SIM). Thus, for each AccelWatch variant, we adopt the model obtained from the Fermi starting point as the final AccelWatch model (Figure 1-(8)).

The other starting point is obtained from the GPUWatch model for NVIDIA Fermi GTX 480 [27] which has been independently validated [21]. Due to having two starting points, we end up with two AccelWatch models. The model obtained from the Fermi starting point achieves higher accuracy (9.2% vs. 14.8% MAPE on the validation set for SASS SIM). Thus, for each AccelWatch variant, we adopt the model obtained from the Fermi starting point as the final AccelWatch model (Figure 1-(8)).

target.markdown: 我们为该过程中初始迭代所使用的缩放因子设置了两种不同的起始点。对于其中一个起始点，将所有初始缩放因子均设置为 1，因此初始阶段不进行任何缩放。另一个起始点则取自针对 NVIDIA Fermi GTX 480 [27] 的 GPUWatch 模型，该模型已得到独立验证 [21]。由于存在两个起始点，我们最终得到了两个 AccelWatch 模型。从 Fermi 起始点得到的模型具有更高的精度（在 SASS SIM 的验证集上，MAPE 为 9.2%，而另一模型为 14.8%）。因此，对于每个 AccelWatch 变体，我们将从 Fermi 起始点得到的模型作为最终的 AccelWatch 模型（图 1-⑧）。

source.markdown: NVML has a low sampling frequency of 50-100 Hz. Thus, we are unable to collect accurate hardware power measurements of short-running kernels (< 2μs run time) because their measurements are perturbed by other events (e.g., invocation/setup overheads to prepare the next kernel iteration, host synchronization, PCI transfers). We exclude such kernels from our suite. We also exclude kernels that are impractical to simulate (> 2 days per run) due to exceedingly-long simulation times and multi-TB instruction trace storage requirements. All kernels are run to completion.

target.markdown: NVML 的采样频率较低，仅为 50–100 Hz。因此，我们无法对短时运行的内核（运行时间 < 2μs）进行精确的硬件功耗测量，因为它们的测量结果会受到其他事件（例如调用/设置开销以准备下一次内核迭代、主机同步、PCI 传输）的干扰。我们将此类内核排除在验证套件之外。同时，由于模拟时间过长以及对多 TB 级指令轨迹存储的需求，我们也排除了那些不切实际、无法模拟的内核（每次运行需要超过 2 天）。所有内核均运行至完成。

# AccelWatch Power vs Measured Power Scatter Plot

## Chart Description

This is a scatter plot comparing **AccelWatch Power (W)** against **Measured Power (W)**. Each blue dot represents a paired measurement. A black diagonal line from origin (0,0) to (270,270) indicates perfect agreement between the two measurements.

## Axes

- **横轴（X轴）**：Measured Power (W) —— 测量功率（单位：瓦特）

- **趋势线**：一条从原点 (0,0) 出发、斜率为 1 的黑色实线（即 y = x），表示理想情况下两变量完全相等。

## 坐标轴刻度与网格

### X轴（Measured Power）
- 范围：0 至 270 W
- 主刻度间隔：30 W（标记值：0, 30, 60, ..., 270）
- 网格线：垂直灰色细线，对应每个主刻度

### Y轴（AccelWatch Power）
- 范围：0 至 270 W

- 网格线：水平灰色细线，对应每个主刻度

> 注：坐标轴形成正方形网格，便于直观比较两个变量的数值关系。

## 数据分布特征

- 所有数据点大致分布在直线 y = x 附近，表明 AccelWatch 记录功率与实测功率具有高度正相关性。
- 多数数据点位于趋势线上下 ±15 W 范围内，说明存在一定测量误差或系统偏差。
- 在低功率区间（< 90 W），数据点较少且分散；中高功率区间（90–240 W）数据点密集，聚集更紧密。
- 最高点约为 (210, 240)，最低非零点约为 (90, 90)。
- 无明显离群点，整体呈线性增长趋势。

## 趋势线说明

- 黑色实线为参考线：**y = x**
  - 表示若 AccelWatch 完全准确，则其读数应等于实测值。
  - 实际数据点围绕该线波动，反映设备精度和一致性。
- 未提供回归拟合线或相关系数（R²），但视觉上可判断 R² > 0.9。

## 初步结论

1. **一致性良好**：AccelWatch 功率读数与实测功率基本一致，适用于大多数应用场景。

source.markdown: Figure 7 shows the correlation plots of the estimated vs. measured power consumption and the corresponding MAPE for AccelWatch SASS SIM and PTX SIM for Volta. Overall, AccelWatch exhibits stronger correlation for SASS than PTX. We attribute this to the fact that PTX instructions do not map 1:1 to SASS instructions; prior work [14] demonstrates that simulating a virtual ISA (PTX) introduces inaccuracies compared to simulating the native ISA (SASS), which directly corresponds to execution on hardware units.

target.markdown: 图 7 展示了 AccelWatch 在 Volta 架构下 SASS SIM 和 PTX SIM 模式的功耗估计值与测量值之间的相关性散点图，以及相应的 MAPE。总体而言，AccelWatch 在 SASS 模式下表现出比 PTX 模式更强的相关性。我们将此归因于以下事实：PTX 指令与 SASS 指令并非一一对应；先前的研究 [14] 表明，与模拟原生 ISA（SASS）相比，模拟虚拟 ISA（PTX）会引入不准确性，而 SASS 直接对应于硬件单元上的执行。

source.markdown: AccelWatch SASS SIM modeling a Volta GV100 compared to hardware measurements attains a MAPE of $9.2\% \pm 3.12\%$ (95% confidence interval) with a maximum relative error of 30%. Two thirds of our validation suite kernels (17 out of 26) have $< 10\%$ absolute relative error, while only 4 kernels have an absolute relative error of $> 20\%$. In comparison, when modeling a Volta architecture, GPUWatch reaches a MAPE of 219% with maximum error 447% (Section 7.3). For the two GPUs it is trained for (GTX 480 and Quadro FX5600), GPUWatch achieves average error of 9.9% and 13.4%, respectively, but with a maximum relative error of 57.8%. Overall, AccelWatch successfully tracks the high variability in measured power across our validation suite (from 90 W up to 230 W).

source.markdown: Among all variants, AccelWatch HW achieves the lowest MAPE (7.5%). This is expected, as it is driven by performance counters collected from execution on real silicon, and does not suffer from the inevitable inaccuracies of software performance models (e.g., AccelSim). However, AccelWatch HW is the most restrictive model, as it does not lend the same modeling flexibility as software simulators.

source.markdown: Figure 8 (left) shows the normalized power breakdown estimated by AccelWatch for Volta averaged across all kernels in the validation set. The register file, static power, and constant power are the most significant power contributors, together consuming 55% of the total system power on average. Volta also has a measurable Idle_SM power component, owing to having a high number of SMs which our validation suite kernels do not always fully utilize. The Others category comprises of the instruction buffer, scheduler, SM pipeline, texture units, and tensor cores (exercised by only 4 out of 26 kernels). As Volta does not have hardware performance counters for register file and L1i, the AccelWatch HW solver minimizes error by lumping their power to other commonly-accessed ones: instruction buffer, scheduler, and SM pipeline. Hence, the Others category grows proportionally to accommodate this reassignment. AccelWatch HYBRID shows a similar trend. Figure 8 also shows that replacing the hardware counters for L2 and NoC hardly changes the power breakdown compared to HW, suggesting that HYBRID is likely to work well when the software model of the targeted component closely approximates its behavior on real silicon.

The Others category comprises of the instruction buffer, scheduler, SM pipeline, texture units, and tensor cores (exercised by only 4 out of 26 kernels). As Volta does not have hardware performance counters for register file and L1i, the AccelWatch HW solver minimizes error by lumping their power to other commonly-accessed ones: instruction buffer, scheduler, and SM pipeline. Hence, the Others category grows proportionally to accommodate this reassignment. AccelWatch HYBRID shows a similar trend. Figure 8 also shows that replacing the hardware counters for L2 and NoC hardly changes the power breakdown compared to HW, suggesting that HYBRID is likely to work well when the software model of the targeted component closely approximates its behavior on real silicon.

target.markdown: 图 8（左）展示了 AccelWatch 针对 Volta 架构所估计的归一化功耗分解，该结果在验证集中的所有内核上进行了平均。寄存器文件、静态功耗和恒定功耗是最主要的功耗贡献者，平均共占总系统功耗的 55%。Volta 还具有可测量的 Idle_SM 功耗分量，这是因为其拥有大量 SM，而我们的验证套件内核并不总是能够充分利用这些 SM。Others 类别包括指令缓冲区、调度器、SM 流水线、纹理单元以及张量核（仅由 26 个内核中的 4 个调用）。由于 Volta 没有针对寄存器文件和 L1i 的硬件性能计数器，AccelWatch HW 求解器通过将其功耗合并到其他经常被访问的组件（即指令缓冲区、调度器和 SM 流水线）中来最小化误差。因此，Others 类别按比例增长以容纳这种重新分配。AccelWatch HYBRID 也呈现出类似的趋势。图 8 还显示，与 HW 相比，替换 L2 和 NoC 的硬件计数器几乎不会改变功耗分解，这表明当目标组件的软件模型接近其在真实硅片上的行为时，HYBRID 很可能表现良好。

source.markdown: Figure 9 shows the power breakdown for each kernel. Tensor cores consume a significant portion of total system power (geomean 28.7%) for the kernels that use them. Note that tensor cores are not part of the Others category in Figure 9. Also, several kernels (backprop_k1, hotspot_k1, sgemm_k1) consume over 90% of the peak power. We postulate this happens because these kernels keep resources busier than the rest due to high thread IPCs (5690, 7157, and 4668, respectively) and have a nearly even split of ALU and FPU (DPU) instructions, which can execute concurrently on Volta.

target.markdown: ### 7.1 对 Pascal 和 Turing 架构的建模

source.markdown: An important goal of an architecture power model is to enable accurate design space exploration. For the use-case scenarios, we envision an architect who starts with the Volta architecture and uses AccelWatch to estimate the power consumption for a new architecture with different parameters. While GPUWatch is configurable, its accuracy when varying parameters has been identified as a weakness [26] (see also Section 7.3). Thus, as our first case study, we apply AccelWatch to estimate the power consumption of two new architectures for which it has not been tuned. We emphasize that if we directly tuned models for these GPUs they would likely result in more accurate models.

target.markdown: 架构功耗模型的一个重要目标是支持准确的设计空间探索。对于这些应用场景，我们设想一位架构师从 Volta 架构开始，并使用 AccelWatch 来估算具有不同参数的新架构的功耗。虽然 GPUWatch 是可配置的，但其参数变化时的准确性已被识别为一个弱点 [26]（另见第 7.3 节）。因此，作为我们的第一个案例研究，我们应用 AccelWatch 来估算两个未经调优的新架构的功耗。我们强调，如果我们直接为这些 GPU 调整模型，它们可能会产生更准确的模型。

source.markdown: Ideally, we would validate AccelWatch predictions for these new architectures against Volta chips that employ these different configurations. However, such chips do not exist. As a proxy, we select configuration parameters similar to the NVIDIA Pascal and Turing architectures, and compare against real Pascal and Turing chips. The Pascal and Turing architectures are the nearest to Volta. Hence, they are the most likely to have similar hardware implementations. Differences in the implementation of hardware units and the ISA between Volta and these architectures will manifest as modeling error. Table 3 lists the parameters of the target GPUs.

target.markdown: 理想情况下，我们应当将 AccelWatch 对这些新架构的预测与采用这些不同配置的 Volta 芯片进行验证。然而，这类芯片并不存在。作为一种替代方案，我们选择与 NVIDIA Pascal 和 Turing 架构相似的配置参数，并与真实的 Pascal 和 Turing 芯片进行比较。Pascal 和 Turing 架构是仅次于 Volta 的架构，因此它们最有可能具有相似的硬件实现。Volta 与这些架构在硬件单元实现和 ISA 上的差异将体现为建模误差。表 3 列出了目标 GPU 的参数。

source.markdown: The evaluation closely follows the validation flow shown in Figure 1-(9), with small modifications. First, the workloads are compiled with compute-capability support for Pascal and Turing (code=sm_61 and code=sm_75 compiler options, respectively). Second, Volta, Pascal and Turing implement different ISAs. Thus, comparing hardware runs on Pascal (or Turing) with Volta-derived traces in Accel-Sim would introduce spurious inaccuracies; we only attempt to model different architectural parameters with Accel-Watch in these use cases after all, not different ISAs. To avoid such spurious inaccuracies, we re-extract traces for Pascal and Turing GPUs to use in the validation of the corresponding use cases. Accel-Watch is still using the Volta-trained model—the traces are used only for validation purposes. Differences in hardware implementations still manifest as errors, as we do not attempt to model different functional unit implementations. We exclude all workloads that use tensor cores (CUTLASS and cudaTensorCoreGemm) from our validation suite for Pascal, since Pascal does not have tensor cores.

target.markdown: 该评估密切遵循图 1-(9) 所示的验证流程，仅作少量修改。首先，工作负载使用针对 Pascal 和 Turing 的计算能力支持进行编译（分别为 code=sm_61 和 code=sm_75 编译器选项）。其次，Volta、Pascal 和 Turing 实现了不同的 ISA。因此，将在 Pascal（或 Turing）上的硬件运行与 Accel-Sim 中源自 Volta 的 trace 进行比较会引入虚假的误差；毕竟在这些用例中，我们只是尝试使用 Accel-Watch 对不同的架构参数进行建模，而不是不同的 ISA。为避免此类虚假误差，我们为 Pascal 和 Turing GPU 重新提取 trace，用于相应用例的验证。Accel-Watch 仍然使用基于 Volta 训练的模型——这些 trace 仅用于验证目的。硬件实现上的差异仍会表现为误差，因为我们并未尝试对不同的功能单元实现进行建模。由于 Pascal 没有张量核，我们将验证套件中所有使用张量核的工作负载（CUTLASS 和 cudaTensorCoreGemm）排除在 Pascal 的验证之外。

source.markdown: AccelWatch is based on the Volta architecture which is implemented at 12 nm, while Pascal is at 16 nm. Thus, following the flow in Figure 1-(9), after we collect power estimates for Pascal from AccelWatch, we apply technology scaling based on published IRDS [17] parameters. Technology scaling reduces MAPE by 1.22%

# GPU Power Comparison: Pascal & Turing vs Volta GV100

## (a) Pascal TITAN X relative to Volta GV100. Error of estimated average relative power: 1%.

### Chart Description:
- **Y-axis**: Relative Power (%) — ranges from -60% to 0%
- **X-axis**: Benchmark kernels (e.g., `b+tree_K1`, `bprop_K2`, ..., `cutlass_K3`, `Avg.`)
- **Legend**:
  - Light blue bar: **Modeled**
  - Dark gray bar: **Measured**
- **Special Note**: For kernel `cTensor_K1`, a red bar indicates “No tensor cores in Pascal”
- **Average Bar (`Avg.`)**: Red bars show modeled and measured average relative power (~ -25% modeled, ~ -30% measured)

### Observations:
- Most benchmarks show negative relative power for both modeled and measured values → Pascal consumes less power than Volta GV100 on these workloads.
- Measured values are generally lower (more negative) than modeled → model underestimates power savings.
- Largest discrepancy observed at `hspot_K1` (measured ≈ -50%, modeled ≈ -35%).
- Kernel `cTensor_K1` is an outlier with no tensor core support in Pascal → marked separately.

---

## (b) Turing RTX 2060S relative to Volta GV100. Error of estimated average relative power: 3%.

### Chart Description:
- **Y-axis**: Relative Power (%) — ranges from -60% to +60%
- **X-axis**: Same benchmark kernels as above
- **Legend**:
  - Light blue bar: **Modeled**
  - Dark gray bar: **Measured**
- **Special Note**: Again, `cTensor_K1` has red bar labeled “No tensor cores in Pascal” — *note: this appears to be a copy-paste error; should likely say “Turing” or refer to lack of comparison baseline*. However, since Turing does have tensor cores, this may indicate missing data or mislabeling.
- **Average Bar (`Avg.`)**: Red bars show small negative values (~ -5% modeled, ~ -7% measured)

### Observations:
- Many benchmarks show positive relative power → Turing sometimes uses *more* power than Volta GV100.
- Notable high-power cases: `bprop_K2` (+70% modeled), `dct_K2` (+30% measured), `histo_K1` (+50% modeled).
- Some kernels show significant power savings: `kmns_K1` (-45% measured), `srad_K1` (-40% modeled).
- Model accuracy varies widely — e.g., `sgemm_K1`: modeled ≈ -10%, measured ≈ -20%; `pfnd_K1`: modeled ≈ +30%, measured ≈ +30% (good match).
- Average relative power is close to zero → overall, Turing’s power consumption is similar to Volta GV100 across these benchmarks.

---

## General Notes Across Both Charts:

- All comparisons are **relative to Volta GV100**, which serves as the baseline (0%).
- “Relative Power” = `(Power_target - Power_Volta) / Power_Volta × 100%`
- Negative value → target GPU uses less power than Volta.
- Positive value → target GPU uses more power than Volta.
- The “Error of estimated average relative power” refers to the difference between modeled and measured average across all benchmarks.
  - Pascal: 1% error → very accurate modeling.
  - Turing: 3% error → slightly less accurate but still reasonable.
- The presence of “No tensor cores in Pascal” for `cTensor_K1` suggests that this kernel relies on tensor operations not available in Pascal architecture — hence, it cannot run natively or requires emulation, leading to anomalous behavior (not plotted or flagged).

---

## Summary Table (Approximate Averages):

| Architecture       | Avg. Modeled Rel. Power | Avg. Measured Rel. Power | Estimation Error |
|--------------------|--------------------------|---------------------------|------------------|
| Pascal TITAN X     | ~ -25%                   | ~ -30%                    | 1%               |
| Turing RTX 2060S   | ~ -5%                    | ~ -7%                     | 3%               |

> ⚠️ Note: In chart (b), the label “No tensor cores in Pascal” next to `cTensor_K1` is likely incorrect — Turing GPUs *do* have tensor cores. This may be a labeling artifact from reusing the same annotation from chart (a). It should probably read “No comparable data” or “Baseline not applicable”.

---

## Conclusion:

- **Pascal TITAN X** consistently shows lower power consumption than Volta GV100 across most benchmarks, with good model fidelity (1% error).
- **Turing RTX 2060S** exhibits mixed results — some kernels use significantly more power, others less — resulting in near-neutral average power difference vs Volta, with moderate model error (3%).
- Tensor-core-dependent kernels (like `cTensor_K1`) behave differently due to architectural differences and require special handling in analysis.

target.markdown: ### 7.2 用于深度学习工作负载的 AccelWattch

source.markdown: GPUs are one of the dominant forces in Machine Learning (ML) acceleration [11]. To assess AccelWatch's accuracy in the ML space, our validation suite already includes workloads from CUTLASS, which primarily consists of general matrix multiply (GEMM) operations. Many operations in modern deep neural networks are either defined as GEMMs or can be cast as such, thus CUTLASS is representative of many ML workloads. In this section we delve deeper into the ML space and evaluate the accuracy of AccelWatch not only in GEMMs, but also in benchmarks implementing Convolutional (CNN) and Recurrent Long-Short Term Memory Neural Networks (RNN-LSTM). For this purpose we use DeepBench [25], a widely-used deep learning benchmark suite.

source.markdown: DeepBench utilizes closed-source, hand-tuned SASS kernels from the cuDNN [8] and cuBLAS [38] libraries, for which there are no PTX representations. While AccelerWatch can execute closed-source kernels and estimate their power consumption, validating AccelerWatch predictions on DeepBench is challenging and error-prone. Each DeepBench workload issues 10–130 kernels (geomean 33), and each kernel only uses about 12 SMs. The GPU hardware executes several kernels concurrently. However, Acceler-Sim executes kernels only sequentially, leaving most of the simulated GPU idle and misleading AccelerWatch to report significantly lower power. This is a limitation of Acceler-Sim and not of AccelerWatch. To mitigate this problem, we hand-construct a possible concurrent kernel

# 功率建模 vs 实测功率对比图

| 标签                  | Measured Power (W) | Modeled Power (W) |

> 注：数值为目测估算，基于网格线和点位相对位置。实际应用中建议结合原始数据源校准。

## 趋势线

- 一条黑色实线从原点 (0, 0) 延伸至右上角 (~240, 240)，代表 y = x 的理想拟合线。
- 多数点位于或接近该线，表明模型在大部分情况下能较好预测实测功率。
- `conv-train` 点显著偏离上方，说明其建模功率远高于实测值（过估计）。
- `conv-inference` 略低于趋势线，说明建模功率略低于实测值（欠估计）。

## 观察结论

1. **线性相关性良好**：除个别点外，整体呈正相关，符合预期。
2. **异常点分析**：
   - `conv-train` 是唯一明显高估的点（建模 240W vs 实测 180W），可能反映训练阶段功耗建模存在系统性偏差。
   - `conv-inference` 轻微低估，但仍在合理误差范围内。
3. **推理 vs 训练**：
   - 推理任务（inference）普遍更贴近趋势线，建模精度更高。
   - 训练任务（train）中 `rnn-lstm-train` 和 `conv-train` 均有不同程度的高估倾向。

source.markdown: To compare AccelWatch with GPUWatch, we apply GPUWatch's Fermi (NVIDIA GTX480) configuration to model Volta. As GPUWatch does not model tensor cores, we enhance it with AccelWatch's estimates for them. In fact, this is our Fermi starting point described in Section 5.4, with updates for the components that GPUWatch does not model (i.e., tensor cores). Running SASS and PTX simulations with this configuration for Volta architectures results in a MAPE of 219% and 225%, respectively, on the same validation suite of kernels. GPUWatch calculates unrealistically high power consumption for all kernels. The average power consumption it estimates is 530 W, with all but three of the kernels scoring above 300 W and a maximum of 926 W.

target.markdown: 为了将 AccelWatch 与 GPUWattch 进行比较，我们采用 GPUWattch 的 Fermi（NVIDIA GTX480）配置来对 Volta 进行建模。由于 GPUWattch 不对张量核进行建模，我们使用 AccelWatch 对张量核的估计来对其进行增强。事实上，这就是我们在第 5.4 节中描述的 Fermi 起点，并针对 GPUWattch 未建模的组件（即张量核）进行了更新。针对 Volta 架构，使用此配置运行 SASS 和 PTX 仿真，在相同的内核验证套件上分别产生了 219% 和 225% 的 MAPE。GPUWattch 对所有内核都计算出了高得离谱的功耗。其估算的平均功耗为 530 W，除三个内核外，其余所有内核的功耗均高于 300 W，最高达到 926 W。

source.markdown: Moreover, in some cases GPUWatch reports unrealistic power consumption for particular components. For example, GPUWatch reports that constant and static power together account for 10.45 W on all validation kernels, which corresponds to 2.4% of the total system power on average. This contradicts our hardware power measurements on Volta, where even the lightest workload possible at the lowest frequency setting consumes >30 W. In addition, GPUWatch estimates that an average 14% of the total system power (including DRAM) is spent on INT_MUL units, compared to 1.4–1.8% in all AccelWatch variants. We believe the high power consumption that GPUWatch attributes to multipliers is unrealistic, as they would consume more power than GPUWatch's estimate for the register file (9.1%), pointing to a GPUWatch inaccuracy. Another notable difference includes GPUWatch's estimate of 27% of the system power spent on DRAM, compared to 8.4–9% in AccelWatch.

target.markdown: 此外，在某些情况下，GPUWattch 会针对特定组件报告不切实际的功耗。例如，GPUWattch 报告在所有验证内核上，恒定功耗与静态功耗之和为 10.45 W，平均占总系统功耗的 2.4%。这与我们在 Volta 上的硬件功耗测量结果相矛盾，因为在最低频率设置下，即使是最轻量级的工作负载，其功耗也超过 30 W。此外，GPUWattch 估计 INT_MUL 单元平均消耗了总系统功耗（含 DRAM）的 14%，而在 AccelWatch 的所有变体中这一比例仅为 1.4–1.8%。我们认为，GPUWattch 将如此高的功耗归因于乘法器是不合理的，因为其消耗的功耗将超过 GPUWattch 对寄存器文件功耗的估计值（9.1%），这表明了 GPUWattch 存在不准确性。另一个值得注意的差异在于，GPUWattch 估计 DRAM 消耗了系统功耗的 27%，而 AccelWatch 的估计仅为 8.4–9%。

source.markdown: GPU architecture research has been largely enabled by event-driven cycle-accurate simulators such as GPGPU-Sim [3], Multi2Sim [44], and MGPU Sim [42]. The lack of a fast, SASS-capable simulator was only recently resolved by Acceler-Sim [20], into which AccelWatch integrates. Validating such tools against real hardware has always been a crucial component of performance modeling research. Similar to our work, prior studies [1, 6, 10, 12, 15, 46] present validation methodologies integrated into contemporary CPU simulators.

source.markdown: The IPP [16] analytic power model achieves high accuracy, but requires source-level PTX analysis that is infeasible for large or closed-source workloads, and PTX may not accurately correspond to real hardware activity [14]. Guerreiro et al. [13] present an analytical model that accurately predicts the power consumption of a GPU given a voltage-frequency setting. However, it provides a fixed power component encompassing static, constant and idle SM power, does not account for component power gating, and can only model architectures with a silicon implementation. AccelWatch is not similarly constrained, and also models 25 microarchitectural power components compared to 8 in Guerreiro et al.

target.markdown: IPP [16] 分析功耗模型具有较高的精度，但需要源代码级别的 PTX 分析，这对于大型或闭源工作负载是不可行的，并且 PTX 可能无法准确对应真实的硬件活动 [14]。Guerreiro 等人 [13] 提出了一种分析模型，能够在给定电压-频率设置的情况下准确预测 GPU 的功耗。然而，该模型将静态功耗、恒定功耗和空闲 SM 功耗统一封装为一个固定的功耗组件，未考虑各组件的功耗门控，并且只能对具有硅实现的架构进行建模。AccelWatch 不受类似限制，并且相较于 Guerreiro 等人的 8 个微架构功耗组件，其建模的组件数量多达 25 个。

source.markdown: In general, analytical models (GPUJoule [2], IPP [16], Guerreiro et al. [13]) can only capture program-level average power consumption, which hinders research that requires cycle-accurate simulation. Meanwhile, AccelWatch can provide a power trace at cycle-level granularity. AccelWatch is the first GPU power model, to the best of our knowledge, to have power components mapped to the SASS machine ISA instructions. Owing to this salient feature, AccelWatch can estimate the power consumption of closed-source GPU workloads that contain hand-tuned assembly.

target.markdown: 总体而言，分析模型（GPUJoule [2]、IPP [16]、Guerreiro 等人 [13]）只能捕获程序级的平均功耗，这阻碍了需要周期精确仿真的研究。而 AccelWatch 能够以周期级粒度提供功耗轨迹。据我们所知，AccelWatch 是第一款将功耗组件映射到 SASS 机器 ISA 指令的 GPU 功耗模型。正是由于这一显著特性，AccelWatch 能够估算包含手工优化汇编代码的闭源 GPU 工作负载的功耗。

target.markdown: ## 9 结论

source.markdown: There is a need for robust tools that will enable GPU architects to quickly model both the performance and the power consumption of modern GPUs. In this paper, we introduce AccelWatch, a configurable cycle-level power model for modern GPUs that can be directed by emulation and trace-driven simulation environments, hardware performance counters, or a combination of the two, striking a balance between model accuracy and performance modeling effort. AccelWatch is the only open-source tool capable of modeling closed-source workloads with hand-tuned SASS instructions.

target.markdown: GPU 架构师需要强大的工具，以便快速建模现代 GPU 的性能和功耗。本文介绍了 AccelWatch，这是一款面向现代 GPU 的可配置周期级功耗模型，可由仿真执行与跟踪驱动模拟环境、硬件性能计数器，或两者的组合驱动，在模型精度与性能建模工作量之间实现平衡。AccelWatch 是唯一能够对包含手工优化 SASS 指令的闭源工作负载进行建模的开源工具。

source.markdown: We infer, for the first time to our knowledge, how modern GPUs power-gate chip-wide, SM-wide and lane-specific hardware components, and introduce an analytic power model that accurately captures the combined effects of power gating, thread divergence, intra-warp functional unit overlap, and variable SM occupancy. We also introduce a DVFS-aware methodology for modeling constant power. We integrate AccelWatch with Accel-Sim and GPGPU-Sim to facilitate its widespread use and release it in the public domain, along with its microbenchmarks and support infrastructure, as an open-source research tool for the computer architecture community. We extensively validate AccelWatch and find that it is within $7.5-9.2 \pm 2.1-3.1\%$ of hardware power measurements on a NVIDIA Volta Quandro GV100 GPU. Finally, we demonstrate that AccelWatch can enable reliable design space exploration.

target.markdown: 据我们所知，本文首次推断出现代 GPU 如何在芯片级、SM 级以及通道级别对硬件组件进行功耗门控，并提出了一种分析功耗模型，能够精确捕捉功耗门控、线程发散、Warp 内功能单元重叠以及可变 SM 占用率所带来的综合效应。我们还提出了一种 DVFS 感知的恒定功耗建模方法。我们将 AccelWatch 与 Accel-Sim 和 GPGPU-Sim 集成，以促进其广泛使用，并将其与微基准测试及配套基础设施一同作为计算机架构社区的开源研究工具发布到公共领域。我们对 AccelWatch 进行了广泛的验证，发现其在 NVIDIA Volta Quandro GV100 GPU 上的硬件功耗测量误差仅为 $7.5-9.2 \pm 2.1-3.1\%$。最后，我们展示了 AccelWatch 能够支持可靠的设计空间探索。

blocks.text: A.3.1 How to access. The artifact, as described in this paper, is archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5398781 under a permissive BSD 2.0 license. To ease the adoption of the tool, we are also in the process of integrating the AccelWatch sources with the latest version of Accel-Sim in the official Accel-Sim GitHub repository at https://github.com/accel-sim/accel-sim-framework, and the sources of the AccelWatch microbenchmarks and validation benchmarks at the official Accel-Sim GPU application collection repository at https://github.com/accel-sim/gpu-app-collection. Interested users should refer to these GitHub links for the latest version of AccelWatch and its support infrastructure.

target.markdown: A.3.1 如何获取。本文中所述的工件已在 Zenodo 上以宽松的 BSD 2.0 许可证归档，地址为 https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5398781。为了便于工具的获取，我们还正在将 AccelWatch 源代码与最新版 Accel-Sim 集成到官方 Accel-Sim GitHub 仓库（https://github.com/accel-sim/accel-sim-framework）中，并将 AccelWatch 微基准测试和验证基准测试的源代码集成到官方 Accel-Sim GPU 应用集合仓库（https://github.com/accel-sim/gpu-app-collection）中。有兴趣的用户应参考这些 GitHub 链接以获取 AccelWatch 及其支持基础设施的最新版本。

source.markdown: A.3.3 *Software dependencies.* AccelWatch uses GCC 7.5.0 and NVCC V11.0 (from Cuda Toolkit 11.0) with nvidia-smi from NVIDIA Driver version 465.19.01. AccelWatch is meant to be run on a modern linux distribution and relies on the same dependencies as the Accel-Sim framework. source.markdown: AccelWatch can estimate power consumption for any CUDA application that is compatible with Accel-Sim simulations. Follow the methodology of Accel-Sim detailed at https://github.com/accelsim/gpu-app-collection/blob/release/README.mdto add a new benchmark to the Accel-Sim framework and run Accel-Sim simulations. AccelWatch power estimatess are then enabled by using a configuration option in Accel-Sim's job launching script run_simulations.py.
